plans.note: Primary cap and exclusions in sec-21; check mutuality, cap multiple/measure (paid vs paid or payable) and whether 'Excluded Claims' (defined in sec-1) properly carves out IP indemnity (sec-20), confidentiality (sec-16), data breach (sec-15/sec-17) and willful misconduct.

Vendor IP and misconduct indemnities expected in sec-20; confirm scope covers third-party IP infringement plus data breach/bodily injury, defence obligations, and that any Customer-side indemnity is narrow. Cross-check sec-14 for IP replacement/modification remedy and sec-1 'Excluded Claims'.

No dedicated restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan sec-12 (Customer responsibilities), sec-2 (scope) and sec-30 (General) for any restriction on competing products or building alternatives before concluding absent.

Check sec-2 for exclusive-supplier or sole-source language and sec-4 (Order Forms/Affiliate Orders) for any requirement that all Affiliate demand route through Vendor; a plain non-exclusivity statement is compliant.
Direction rule: look in sec-7 (Fees/pricing) and sec-4 for any obligation that we offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others; MFN running in our favour needs no comment.
Likely buried in sec-30 (General) if present; if found, confirm mutuality, term of 12 months or less, personnel-specific scope and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out.

Termination triggers in sec-9; verify Customer convenience right on notice without termination fees, and that Vendor has no symmetrical convenience right mid-term. Check sec-10 and sec-7 for early-termination charges or non-refund language.
Auto-renewal mechanics and non-renewal notice window in sec-8; check window length (30-60 days preferred) and any renewal price uplift cap in sec-8 or sec-7.
sec-28 governs; confirm law is NY/DE/CA/England & Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign-seat arbitration. Note escalation/mediation steps in rationale only.
sec-24 covers assignment and change of control; confirm we may assign to Affiliates and to a successor by merger/asset sale without consent, and that Vendor cannot terminate on our change of control.

Deliverable ownership in sec-14 and Customer Data ownership in sec-15; check for any assignment of our IP/data to Vendor, broad feedback or aggregated-data/derivative rights, and confirm a licence-back to us where Vendor retains Vendor Technology (sec-13, sec-1 definitions).

Access/licence grant in sec-13; confirm it extends to our Affiliates and contractors, covers the Order Form term, and is not revocable at Vendor's discretion (check suspension rights in sec-9 or sec-13).

sec-22 is the Vendor-side audit of our usage: check frequency (max once per 12 months), advance written notice, business-hours/remote-first conduct, Vendor bears cost absent material shortfall, and confidentiality of results. sec-23 may hold our reciprocal assurance/records rights.
Direction rule: service credits in sec-3 favour us and need no comment; look for interest/late fees, penalties or liquidated damages payable by us in sec-7, and early-termination penalties in sec-9.

sec-19 warranties: check duration (90 days minimum, preferably term-long for services), professional/workmanlike standard, and a real remedy (re-performance then refund). Cross-reference acceptance testing in sec-6 and service levels in sec-3, and watch for broad disclaimers of implied warranties.
sec-18 present; verify coverage lines and limits (commercial general liability, professional/E&O, cyber) plus certificates on request and notice of cancellation.

Check sec-4 and sec-7 for minimum volume/take-or-pay commitments, non-reducible seat counts or no-downgrade language at renewal; acceptable if paired with an exit or reduction right (cross-check sec-8/sec-9).

sec-11 covers transition assistance and data return; confirm minimum assistance period, machine-readable export of Customer Data at no or reasonable cost, and that assistance is not conditioned on our being fully paid up or on Vendor's discretion (check sec-10 effects and sec-15 deletion obligations).
